newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries in London stable ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries in London stable ahead of data.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices in London on Thursday were stable ahead of a clutch of data which will be watched closely for pointers to inflation.

Richard Gibbs, futures broker at Cater Allen, said attention would focus mainly on the October consumer prices figure at 1330 GMT. The market consensus here is for a rise of 0.3 percent, the same as September.

"The Fed didn't move on Wednesday so we assume that they knew the numbers and are quite happy with things," said Gibbs, referring to the Federal Open Market Committee meeting which left interest rates unchanged.
The U.S. long bond at 1126 GMT was at 100-13 yielding 6.469 percent, unchanged from the Tokyo close and compared with 100-20 at Wednesday's close in New York.
December T-bond futures were at 114-17, 6/32 down on the Wednesday Chicago settlement.

As well as the inflation figure, Gibbs said traders would be looking at retail sales for October, forecast at a 0.3 percent rise after a 0.7 percent jump in September, plus latest weekly jobless claims, seen at 334,000 against 331,000 last time.
Gibbs described trade in London ahead of the data as "pretty light" with the greatest focus on the long end.
"The short end is laid back and has priced in that there will not be a rate rise probably this side of March next year," he said.
Michael Burke, senior economist at Citibank, agreed the market was positioned as though there would be no rate rise for some time.

However, he said he did not share the market's optimism on this score and said the consensus view could be upset by a surprise on the data, if not on Thursday then in the coming weeks or months. -- Stephen Nisbet, International Bonds Unit +44 171 6320
